buildSourceNote: Build 149 carries v1.1.0-rc.26 and completes the chain that lets a technician actually be paid. THE OWNER'S RULE, stated on 2026-09-18: the split is added and calculated once the invoice is uploaded. The invoice is the document that carries BOTH the labour figure and the technician list, so it is where attribution can finally be derived for a job that already exists. Two of the three pieces were already present and the middle was missing: the OCR extractor already asked the model for labour_amount AND assigned_technicians, and the ProductivityCalculator already mapped those names to employee ids and called assign then revenue - but POST /api/job-cards/:jobId/invoice-ocr accepted only { ocrText }, the raw text blob, and discarded every parsed field, so nothing downstream could use them. That endpoint had also never been called once in production: invoice_ocr_data is NULL on all 671 job cards. It now accepts invoice_no, labour_amount, parts_amount and assigned_technicians, persists them, and when a labour_amount is supplied it attributes the job and writes the split through the existing transactional writer. A call without a labour_amount behaves exactly as it always did. TECHNICIAN SOURCE: the invoice's name list wins, but ONLY when every name resolves. It is the only route to a two-technician job, because job_card_master.assigned_to is a single scalar - so without it the 60/40 shipped in build 147 and the mechanic/electrician 50/50 shipped in build 148 could never apply to anything. Names are matched conservatively: exact full-name match, else a substring match only if exactly one employee matches, else the name is reported and the invoice list is refused in favour of assigned_to. A partial match is refused rather than used, because allocating to only some of the people named on an invoice would silently over-pay them. THE ENDPOINT HAD NO AUTHORIZATION GUARD OF ITS OWN; it now uses jobCardEditGuard, the same audited guard as /:id/revenue, rather than a second divergent check, and that guard now accepts either :id or :jobId on the same route. It still fails closed. EAR-001 FIXES in the same path: extractInvoiceWithAzure returned INV- plus a timestamp as an invoice number, JC000 as a job card number, and the placeholders Walk-in Customer and Unknown whenever parsing failed - a generated invoice number is indistinguishable from a real one once stored, and this endpoint now writes invoice_no to the database, so every unreadable field is null with extraction_failed true; ProductivityCalculator generated an INV- random and a JC- random for the same reason and those were written back to the job card. TESTS: 92 passing across four suites, including the ambiguity refusal where two real technicians share an MD prefix, and two end-to-end cases reaching the multi-technician rules for the first time - a two-mechanic invoice producing 60/40 and a mechanic plus electrician invoice producing 50/50. GATES: lint:fabrication PASS (892 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings); tsc --noEmit clean on every file this build touches. NOT ADDRESSED, deliberately, because each is historical and money-bearing: the 123 job cards whose assigned_to holds the creator id 74 rather than a technician, no employee 74 exists, and the 442 completed GATE_OUT jobs - 404 of them with a resolvable technician and 22.9 lakh of recorded revenue - that have no attribution at all. ALSO STILL OPEN from rc.24: the served /version.json reports build 127 because it is copied from public/version.json, a different file with a different schema that no release step updates.
